pathway.title: Uniti Group Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Recurring revenue is shrinking faster than fiber growth replaces it, which is the root of the credit's weakness. On a pro forma basis service revenue fell USD 83.6 million, or 8.93%, in Q2 2026 and USD 159.0 million, or 8.36%, in the first half, as legacy copper, voice and TDM losses at Kinetic (USD 59.6 million) and Uniti Solutions (USD 37.0 million) outweighed a USD 13.0 million gain at Fiber Infrastructure. Total revenue fell only USD 48.7 million, or 5.08%, in Q2 because sales revenue rose USD 34.9 million, so headline revenue overstates the recurring base that services the debt. Basis: calculation C6; 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 73–74

Free cash flow is structurally negative while the build runs, and borrowing fills the gap. Capital expenditures of USD 799.2 million exceeded operating cash flow of USD 339.4 million in the first half of 2026, a free cash outflow of USD 459.8 million after USD 437.6 million in FY2025, and net debt issuance was USD 1,142.6 million. The quarterly report credits deferred-revenue timing for part of the improvement in operating cash flow and Fiber Infrastructure received upfront customer payments of USD 162.1 million, so the reported outflow may flatter the underlying position; the split is not stated. Basis: calculation C3; calculation C12; calculation C14; 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 84; EX-99.1_2026-05-11_unit-ex9911q26.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-07-30_unit-ex9912q26.htm.jsonl, page 2

Leverage is high and the reported ratio hides it. Total debt is 7.13x and net debt 6.73x trailing adjusted EBITDA, against 3.64x on reported EBITDA, which keeps a USD 1,683.9 million non-cash merger gain, and adjusted EBITDA covers cash interest 1.94x against 1.78x for FY2025. The trailing figure omits Windstream's earnings for July 2025 and the issuer prints no full-year pro forma ratio, so like-for-like leverage would be modestly lower. Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; Financial foundation (CP-1)

The 2026 outlook implies a weaker second half than the first. The midpoint of the adjusted EBITDA outlook of USD 1,450 million to USD 1,500 million leaves USD 676.3 million for the second half against USD 798.7 million earned in the first half, or USD 338.15 million a quarter against USD 357.1 million in Q2, while the net loss outlook midpoint has widened from USD 385.0 million in March to USD 505.0 million in July and the net interest expense outlook has risen from USD 775 million to USD 805 million. The first quarter was lifted by sales-type lease revenue, so management's own range does not assume earnings growth from the second-quarter level. Basis: calculation C7; calculation C13; EX-99.1_2026-07-30_unit-ex9912q26.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-03-02_unit-ex991202510xk.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-05-11_unit-ex9911q26.htm.jsonl, page 2

Liquidity is adequate to 2028 but depends on revolvers that expire in December 2027. Cash of USD 608.9 million and undrawn revolver capacity of USD 838.1 million total USD 1,447.0 million, which is 1.61 times the USD 896.5 million due in 2027 and 2028, but cash fell USD 373.7 million in Q2 and the Windstream Revolver commitment falls from USD 475.0 million to USD 425.0 million after January 23, 2027. Management states that cash, operating cash flow and revolver capacity cover the next twelve months and beyond; the net proceeds of the July 2026 securitization are not stated. Basis: calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C18; 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 23–24; 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 83; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Refinancing risk is back-ended but heavy. Maturities are small to 2028, at USD 5.0 million in 2026, USD 316.5 million in 2027 and USD 580.0 million in 2028, then USD 7,360.1 million, or 68.91% of principal, falls in 2031 to 2033, including USD 2,200.0 million of the 2031 secured notes, USD 1,600.0 million of the 2032 unsecured notes and USD 1,400.0 million of the 2033 secured notes. The securitization notes fall at anticipated repayment dates, so those amounts depend on market access rather than on cash generation. Basis: calculation C5; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 30

Securitization is the funding valve, and it moves collateral away from other creditors. Notes of USD 1,799.1 million, or 16.84% of principal, sit at unrestricted subsidiaries that no other group entity guarantees, and USD 1,140.7 million more was issued in July 2026 at a weighted average coupon of about 6.18% to buy assets held by guarantor subsidiaries. In the first half the unrestricted subsidiaries earned operating income plus depreciation and amortization of USD 133.4 million on interest of USD 51.9 million, a cover of 2.57x, while the restricted group earned USD 605.4 million on interest of USD 332.0 million, 1.82x, so the creditors with claims on the restricted group carry the weaker coverage. Basis: calculation C8; calculation C9; 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 51; 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 52–54; EX-99.1_2026-07-30_unit-ex9912q26.htm.jsonl, page 2; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Fiber demand is real, which supports the long-run case but does not yet fund the debt. Consumer fiber revenue grew 19% pro forma in Q2 2026, consumer fiber net additions and premises constructed were records, Fiber Infrastructure new bookings reached a record USD 2.2 million of monthly recurring revenue, and remaining performance obligations were about USD 2.3 billion at year-end. Fiber was still only 43.19% of FY2025 Kinetic consumer revenue, so conversion has years to run before it offsets legacy declines. Basis: calculation C10; EX-99.1_2026-07-30_unit-ex9912q26.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-K_2025-12-31_unit-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 161

Subsidy-linked build commitments add execution risk. Uniti missed a 40% completion milestone for its rural broadband awards in some states because of permitting delays and notified the regulator in January 2026; the annual report says missed milestones could lead to withheld future funding or recovery of support already paid, the outcome for Uniti is not stated, and only USD 9.8 million of the USD 184.3 million of new federal broadband awards is under executed contracts. Grant support of USD 160.6 million for further builds is secured, so funding helps the build but does not remove the cash outflow. Basis: calculation C17; 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 81–82; 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 87; 10-K_2025-12-31_unit-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 163

Governance adds leakage rather than control risk. Preferred stock with a liquidation preference of USD 575.0 million pays 11%, about USD 63.25 million a year, and steps up to a cap of 16%; USD 31.2 million was declared in the first half of 2026 against USD 16.7 million paid in cash. Elliott holds about 25.2% of the common stock and may designate two directors, no common dividend is expected, and Elliott's affiliates can require repurchase of the preferred stock after the tenth anniversary at its liquidation preference. Basis: calculation C11; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_unit-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-K_2025-12-31_unit-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-K_2025-12-31_unit-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 106; 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 85

runs.text: The first strength is liquidity and near-term maturity cover. Cash and undrawn revolvers of USD 1,447.0 million are 1.61 times the USD 896.5 million due in 2027 and 2028, which keeps a refinancing event out of the next two years unless the revolvers expire unrenewed in December 2027. Basis: calculation C4; calculation C5; 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 83

The second strength is demonstrated capital-market access. Uniti has raised almost USD 3 billion through asset securitizations and priced the July 2026 notes at a weighted average coupon of about 6.18%, so the build can be financed while the market stays open, though each issue moves assets away from other creditors. Basis: calculation C8; EX-99.1_2026-07-30_unit-ex9912q26.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2

The third strength is contracted and growing fiber demand. Consumer fiber revenue grew 19% pro forma in Q2 2026, Fiber Infrastructure new bookings reached a record USD 2.2 million of monthly recurring revenue, and remaining performance obligations were about USD 2.3 billion, which supports higher-quality recurring earnings once the legacy base stabilizes. Basis: calculation C10; EX-99.1_2026-07-30_unit-ex9912q26.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-K_2025-12-31_unit-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 161

The fourth strength is limited interest-rate exposure. Only USD 345.0 million of floating-rate debt is unhedged and a 100 bp rise would add USD 3.5 million of annual interest, so cash interest is largely fixed and predictable against a base of fixed coupons. Basis: calculation C16; 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 92

The fifth strength is scale and customer diversification. No customer exceeds 10% of revenue after the merger and Kinetic's contribution margin stayed above 42% in each of the last three quarters, so no single contract or customer decides debt service. Basis: calculation C15; 10-K_2025-12-31_unit-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; EX-99.1_2026-07-30_unit-ex9912q26.htm.jsonl, page 2

The first weakness is negative free cash flow funded by debt. The first-half outflow of USD 459.8 million and net debt issuance of USD 1,142.6 million mean leverage cannot fall through cash generation, so creditors rely on market access until the build ends. Basis: calculation C3; 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 6

The second weakness is shrinking recurring service revenue. Pro forma service revenue fell 8.93% in Q2 2026 while sales-type lease revenue masked the decline in total revenue, so the base that services the debt is smaller than headline revenue suggests. Basis: calculation C6; 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 73–74

The third weakness is high leverage and thin cover. Total debt of 7.13x adjusted EBITDA and cash interest cover of 1.94x leave little room if second-half earnings come in at the implied USD 676.3 million, where cover on net interest would be 1.61x. Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C7; Financial foundation (CP-1)

The fourth weakness is a heavy back-ended wall that rests on securitization. USD 7,360.1 million, or 68.91% of principal, falls in 2031 to 2033, and ring-fenced notes of USD 1,799.1 million, plus USD 1,140.7 million issued in July 2026, give the restricted group less collateral and weaker cover of 1.82x. Basis: calculation C5; calculation C8; calculation C9; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 50–54

The fifth weakness is preferred stock and subsidy execution. The preferred stock takes about USD 63.25 million a year and steps up to a 16% cap, and missed completion milestones for rural broadband awards and uncontracted federal awards leave subsidy income uncertain. Basis: calculation C11; calculation C17; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_unit-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-K_2025-12-31_unit-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 106; 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 81–82

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The Windstream merger closed on August 1, 2025 as a reverse merger: Old Uniti was the accounting acquirer and Windstream the legal acquirer, with pre-closing holders of Old Uniti and Windstream owning about 62% and 38% before convertible securities. Windstream's equityholders received about 90.1 million common shares, 35.42% of the common, about 0.6 million non-voting preferred shares with an 11% dividend and a liquidation preference of USD 575.0 million, about 17.6 million penny warrants and about USD 370.7 million of cash, the cash funded from Old Uniti's cash and revolver borrowings. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_unit-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6; 10-K_2025-12-31_unit-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 106

On August 4, 2025 Uniti Group LP merged into Uniti Services LLC, so one borrower carries the debt of both legacy groups, each group's guarantors now guarantee the other's debt, the Windstream revolver became pari passu with the other first lien debt and the restrictive covenants that kept the two groups apart were effectively eliminated. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_unit-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 56; 10-K_2025-12-31_unit-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 139

In October 2025 Uniti Services issued USD 1.4 billion of 7.50% senior secured notes due 2033 and borrowed a new USD 1.0 billion seven-year term loan, using the proceeds to redeem the 10.50% secured notes in full at a redemption premium of USD 119.5 million, and the ABS notes issuers sold USD 250.0 million of secured fiber network revenue term notes. In 2026 the Kinetic ABS issuer sold USD 960.1 million of notes in January, and Uniti Services issued an additional USD 1.0 billion of 8.625% unsecured notes and repaid its USD 500.0 million Windstream term loan in February. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_unit-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 145–146; 10-K_2025-12-31_unit-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 151; 10-K_2025-12-31_unit-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 149; 10-K_2025-12-31_unit-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 195; 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 30

After the June 30, 2026 balance sheet, the Kinetic ABS issuer sold about USD 1.1 billion of Series 2026-2 notes on July 15, 2026 to buy assets held by guarantor subsidiaries, and on July 23, 2026 Uniti Services offered to prepay up to USD 167.8 million of the 2025 term loan while the secured notes' issuers offered to buy up to USD 332.2 million of their notes, together USD 500.0 million; USD 19.8 million of the term loan was repaid on July 30, 2026 and the results of the other offers are not reported. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 52–54; EX-99.1_2026-07-30_unit-ex9912q26.htm.jsonl, page 2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business and governance facts for Uniti Group Inc. (issuer id unit) as of 2026-11-05 on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the business, ownership, governance, transactions and issuer history that matter to a creditor, drawn from the seven supplied filings and releases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The supplied earlier result is Source readiness (CP-0), sha256 64d248a13b0335b24ecac42da4c70f0c4d2a0ef3b5a389c76e6e8a0437811bcf. Its statement that ownership concentration is not established is corrected in this module: the annual report's risk factors state it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Uniti is a debt-heavy turnaround under concentrated but non-controlling ownership: creditor risk rests on a debt-funded fiber build and on board decisions over collateral and financing, not on a sponsor's distribution record.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Elliott holds about 25.2% of the common stock with a right to designate two of the nine directors, the two largest holders and insiders hold about 36.1%, and preferred stock paying 11% with a liquidation preference of USD 575.0 million ranks ahead of the common. A July 2026 securitization moved assets out of guarantor subsidiaries into unrestricted subsidiaries, partly offset by up to USD 500.0 million of secured debt repayment offers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Compensation, related-party and board-independence detail sit in a proxy statement that is not in the sources, so the governance view rests on the annual report and quarterly filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business changed in kind in August 2025. Old Uniti was a REIT whose tenant Windstream paid 68.3% of revenue; the combined company earns 56.14% of first-half 2026 revenue from Kinetic broadband, 24.27% from Fiber Infrastructure and 19.59% from Uniti Solutions, and no customer reached 10% of revenue after the merger, so single-tenant dependence has gone but legacy copper decline now drives the base.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C2; 10-K_2025-12-31_unit-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_unit-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6; 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 47–48

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fiber build is the credit's central bet and it is not yet self-funding. Consumer fiber subscriber revenue was USD 195.4 million in FY2025 against USD 257.0 million of legacy DSL and other consumer revenue, and capital expenditures of USD 799.2 million in the first half of 2026 exceeded operating cash flow of USD 339.4 million, with the fiber build targeted to run to the end of 2029 (customer, household and passing counts are in the operating model table).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fiber Infrastructure revenue is lumpy. A dark fiber IRU sold to a hyperscaler added USD 85.5 million of sales revenue in the first half of 2026, recognised up front as a sales-type lease, so first quarter 2026 revenue of USD 987.5 million, against USD 909.7 million in the second quarter, should not be read as a run rate.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ownership is concentrated but not controlling, and control rights are specific. Elliott may designate two directors for as long as it holds at least half of its original shares, the certificate waives corporate opportunities for significant holders, and affiliates of Elliott may require repurchase of the preferred stock after the tenth anniversary of issue at the liquidation preference of USD 575.0 million plus accrued dividends; none of this is evidence of how holders will behave toward creditors.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Creditor claims sit in layers and one layer is growing. Credit facilities and secured notes share first-priority collateral under an intercreditor agreement, unsecured notes are effectively subordinated, and USD 1,799.1 million of ABS notes at unrestricted subsidiaries are ring-fenced from other creditors; the July 2026 Kinetic securitization added further assets to that pool.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C6; 10-K_2025-12-31_unit-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 144; 10-K_2025-12-31_unit-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 201; 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 52–54

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Disclosure is audited and controls were reported effective, which supports monitoring. The 2025 annual report carries a PricewaterhouseCoopers opinion on the statements and on internal control, the auditor changed from KPMG for 2025, and common dividends are not expected while preferred dividends of USD 31.2 million were declared in the first half of 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a lower governance risk is that no distribution to shareholders is documented since the merger, the 10.50% secured notes were redeemed in full in October 2025 and replaced by longer-dated debt, and the July 2026 securitization carried a weighted average coupon of about 6.18% with USD 500.0 million of proceeds offered to repay secured debt. The view would improve if the offers retire that amount and the unrestricted pool stops growing. It would worsen if more guarantor-held assets move into unrestricted subsidiaries without matching repayment, if Elliott's 25.2% stake is used to alter the board or the preferred stock is put after the tenth anniversary, or if the executed debt documents show capacity for further transfers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The sources do not state the capacity in the debt documents for moving assets to unrestricted subsidiaries, so the July 2026 transfer is recorded as an action and not as evidence of intent; the executed indentures would settle it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Compensation, related-party transactions, board independence and holders below the two largest are in a proxy statement that is not in the sources, so the governance view could change on any of them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Results of the July 2026 repayment offers and any event after July 30, 2026 are not in the sources, so whether the securitization was creditor-neutral is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Segment and revenue figures are recast after the merger and earlier periods are Old Uniti only, so the 68.3% tenant share and the segment mix before August 2025 are not like-for-like with later periods.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Customer and household counts are approximate figures stated by the issuer, so the fiber penetration trend is indicative only.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The Windstream merger closed on August 1, 2025 as a reverse merger: Old Uniti was the accounting acquirer and Windstream the legal acquirer, with pre-closing holders of Old Uniti and Windstream owning about 62% and 38% before convertible securities. Windstream's equityholders received about 90.1 million common shares, 35.42% of the common, about 0.6 million non-voting preferred shares with an 11% dividend and a liquidation preference of USD 575.0 million, about 17.6 million penny warrants and about USD 370.7 million of cash, the cash funded from Old Uniti's cash and revolver borrowings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On August 4, 2025 Uniti Group LP merged into Uniti Services LLC, so one borrower carries the debt of both legacy groups, each group's guarantors now guarantee the other's debt, the Windstream revolver became pari passu with the other first lien debt and the restrictive covenants that kept the two groups apart were effectively eliminated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In October 2025 Uniti Services issued USD 1.4 billion of 7.50% senior secured notes due 2033 and borrowed a new USD 1.0 billion seven-year term loan, using the proceeds to redeem the 10.50% secured notes in full at a redemption premium of USD 119.5 million, and the ABS notes issuers sold USD 250.0 million of secured fiber network revenue term notes. In 2026 the Kinetic ABS issuer sold USD 960.1 million of notes in January, and Uniti Services issued an additional USD 1.0 billion of 8.625% unsecured notes and repaid its USD 500.0 million Windstream term loan in February.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: After the June 30, 2026 balance sheet, the Kinetic ABS issuer sold about USD 1.1 billion of Series 2026-2 notes on July 15, 2026 to buy assets held by guarantor subsidiaries, and on July 23, 2026 Uniti Services offered to prepay up to USD 167.8 million of the 2025 term loan while the secured notes' issuers offered to buy up to USD 332.2 million of their notes, together USD 500.0 million; USD 19.8 million of the term loan was repaid on July 30, 2026 and the results of the other offers are not reported.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor and governance risk level: Medium. The level is driven by concentrated ownership with board rights and by assets moving to unrestricted subsidiaries, because they reduce the collateral available to creditors outside the ABS issuers, which raises their expected loss in a default; countervailing evidence is the absence of documented distributions and the 500.0 repayment offer.

fields.value: Recurring revenue is shrinking faster than fiber growth replaces it, which is the root of the credit's weakness. On a pro forma basis service revenue fell USD 83.6 million, or 8.93%, in Q2 2026 and USD 159.0 million, or 8.36%, in the first half, as legacy copper, voice and TDM losses at Kinetic (USD 59.6 million) and Uniti Solutions (USD 37.0 million) outweighed a USD 13.0 million gain at Fiber Infrastructure. Total revenue fell only USD 48.7 million, or 5.08%, in Q2 because sales revenue rose USD 34.9 million, so headline revenue overstates the recurring base that services the debt.

fields.value: Free cash flow is structurally negative while the build runs, and borrowing fills the gap. Capital expenditures of USD 799.2 million exceeded operating cash flow of USD 339.4 million in the first half of 2026, a free cash outflow of USD 459.8 million after USD 437.6 million in FY2025, and net debt issuance was USD 1,142.6 million. The quarterly report credits deferred-revenue timing for part of the improvement in operating cash flow and Fiber Infrastructure received upfront customer payments of USD 162.1 million, so the reported outflow may flatter the underlying position; the split is not stated.

fields.value: The strongest evidence for a better view is rising earnings guidance together with cheaper secured funding. Management raised the 2026 adjusted EBITDA outlook midpoint by USD 25.0 million between March and July, consumer fiber revenue is growing at 19% pro forma, and the July 2026 securitization carried a weighted average coupon of about 6.18% against 8.25% on the 2031 secured notes, so the cost of capital is falling as the securitization market absorbs the build. Floating-rate exposure is small, with USD 345.0 million unhedged and USD 3.5 million of added annual interest for a 100 bp rise, and management states that liquidity covers the next twelve months and beyond. The view would improve if service revenue declines narrow toward the low single digits, adjusted EBITDA exceeds the top of the outlook range, free cash flow after grant funding turns positive, the secured repayment offers retire the full USD 500.0 million and both revolvers are extended beyond 2027. It would worsen if second-half adjusted EBITDA falls below the USD 676.3 million implied by the outlook midpoint, further guarantor assets move into the ring-fenced pool without matching repayment, or a securitization or revolver extension cannot be completed on similar terms.

Source readiness says ownership concentration is not established, and Business & governance corrects that from the annual report's risk factors. Financial foundation records the USD 1.5 million gap between the full-year and nine-month merger gain as unexplained, and the fourth quarter reconciliation in the results release shows a USD 1.5 million reduction that accounts for it. Financial foundation gives the year-end fiber customer count only as a lower bound, while the annual report states an approximate figure that is recorded in the source register.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-03-02_unit-ex991202510xk.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_unit-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 59

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Uniti is a three-segment fiber and broadband operator formed by the August 2025 merger of Old Uniti and Windstream. Kinetic sells broadband and voice to consumers, businesses and wholesale buyers in former Windstream markets, Fiber Infrastructure leases dark and lit fiber, mainly to carriers and hyperscalers, and Uniti Solutions sells managed network services to enterprises. First-half 2026 revenue of USD 1,897.2 million was 56.14% Kinetic, 24.27% Fiber Infrastructure and 19.59% Uniti Solutions, and no customer exceeds 10% of revenue after the merger, which removes the single-tenant dependence that gave Windstream 68.3% of Old Uniti's revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C19; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_unit-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 47–48

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The mix supports cash-flow visibility only in part. Fiber Infrastructure and managed services rest on contracts, with remaining performance obligations of about USD 2.3 billion at year-end, whereas Kinetic's consumer base faces cable, fiber overbuilders, fixed wireless and satellite competition and is losing copper customers. The credit consequence is that debt service depends on Kinetic's conversion from copper to fiber and on contract renewals at Fiber Infrastructure, not on lease income, which ended with the merger.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C10; 10-K_2025-12-31_unit-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_unit-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 161; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ownership is concentrated but not controlling. Elliott holds about 25.2% of the common stock and may designate two of nine directors, the two largest holders and insiders hold about 36.1%, and Old Uniti's five-member board forms the board majority. The credit facilities and notes are issued by Uniti Services LLC and its finance subsidiaries, with the credit facilities guaranteed by Uniti Group Inc., Old Uniti and subsidiary guarantors, while the asset-backed notes sit at bankruptcy-remote unrestricted subsidiaries that no other group entity guarantees. The credit consequence is that financial policy follows a board that has chosen debt and securitization to fund the build, with no sponsor support or equity cure evidenced.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_unit-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-K_2025-12-31_unit-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 106; 10-K_2025-12-31_unit-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 144; 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 50–51

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The capacity for further transfers to unrestricted subsidiaries, restricted payments and liens is not established because the executed credit agreements and indentures are not supplied, so the July 2026 transfer is recorded as an action and no sponsor willingness is inferred.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is structurally declining at Kinetic and Uniti Solutions, growing at Fiber Infrastructure and lumpy through sales-type leases. Pro forma service revenue fell USD 83.6 million in Q2 2026, and the USD 13.0 million gain at Fiber Infrastructure came mainly from price increases for transport and TDM services and favorable reserve adjustments, which are not repeatable volume growth. Consumer fiber revenue grew 19%, but the DSL base that it replaces is still larger than fiber revenue in FY2025, and customer bankruptcies in Q2 pushed credit loss provisions up by USD 12.1 million. The credit consequence is that pricing power is limited to the fiber product and the contract base, so earnings durability rests on the conversion pace.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C6; calculation C10; 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 67; 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 73–74; 10-K_2025-12-31_unit-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 161

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins are under pressure because costs fall more slowly than revenue. Pro forma cost of services fell USD 29.7 million in Q2 2026 against a USD 83.6 million fall in service revenue, a cost response of 35.53%, and selling, general and administrative cost rose USD 12.9 million. Kinetic contribution margin eased from 44.14% in Q4 2025 to 42.97% in Q1 2026 and 42.37% in Q2 2026 as its revenue fell from USD 558.7 million to USD 539.0 million, and the consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin was 39.25% in Q2 against 44.72% in Q1, when sales-type lease revenue lifted earnings. The credit consequence is that margin defence depends on the fiber mix and not on cost cuts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C15; calculation C6; 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 73; EX-99.1_2026-03-02_unit-ex991202510xk.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-05-11_unit-ex9911q26.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-07-30_unit-ex9912q26.htm.jsonl, page 2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Adjusted EBITDA does not convert to free cash flow while the build runs. Operating cash flow was 42.49% of first-half adjusted EBITDA and capital expenditures were 100.06% of it, with Kinetic taking 77.98% of the USD 450.0 million spent in Q2 and capital expenditure running at 1.54 times Kinetic's quarterly contribution margin. Grants funded USD 34.8 million of spending in the half and USD 11.9 million of grant funds were received, and further builds carry grant support of USD 160.6 million against incremental capital expenditure of USD 131.9 million. The credit consequence is that deleveraging by cash flow is not available until the build ends, and the share of spending that is optional is not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C14; calculation C15; calculation C17; 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 84; 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 87; EX-99.1_2026-07-30_unit-ex9912q26.htm.jsonl, page 2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry and substitutes press the legacy base hardest. The annual report names cable operators as the largest competitor for residential and small business broadband, with fiber overbuilders including utilities and municipalities, fixed wireless and satellite all increasing, and says few locations in the footprint lack meaningful competition. Cable and wireless pricing keep churn pressure on copper customers, which is why service revenue falls, and entrants add to the cost of the fiber build because customers must be won rather than inherited.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Buyer power is concentrated at Fiber Infrastructure, where hyperscalers and large carriers negotiate large contracts and some customers pay upfront, and where enterprise competitors include national carriers, cable operators and managed service providers. Supplier power is not established from the sources. The credit consequence is that Fiber Infrastructure earnings are strong but lumpy and renewal-dependent, while Kinetic competes for every subscriber.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Regulation and subsidy policy are material, macroeconomic and technology factors less so. The rural broadband award of USD 522.8 million over ten years carries completion milestones that were missed in some states, with withholding or recovery of support possible, new federal broadband awards of USD 184.3 million are only partly contracted, and state universal service support of USD 25.2 million in the first half includes a Pennsylvania program under regulatory review. Hyperscaler demand for fiber is the main technology tailwind. Rates matter little to the interest bill because only USD 345.0 million of floating debt is unhedged. The credit consequence is that subsidy timing can move capital needs and earnings, but no single policy event decides the credit.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C16; calculation C17; 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 81–82; 10-K_2025-12-31_unit-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 163; 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 92

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths are national fiber scale, contracted fiber demand, demonstrated market access and liquidity of USD 1,447.0 million that covers the 2027 and 2028 maturities. Weaknesses are leverage of 7.13x, negative free cash flow, shrinking service revenue and thin cash interest cover of 1.94x. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are subsidy funding for the build, the monetization of non-core assets that management says it may seek, and fiber conversion lifting recurring revenue. Threats are cable and wireless competition, a securitization window that closes, revolvers that expire in December 2027 and further collateral transfers to unrestricted subsidiaries.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 83; EX-99.1_2026-07-30_unit-ex9912q26.htm.jsonl, page 1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first strength is liquidity and near-term maturity cover. Cash and undrawn revolvers of USD 1,447.0 million are 1.61 times the USD 896.5 million due in 2027 and 2028, which keeps a refinancing event out of the next two years unless the revolvers expire unrenewed in December 2027.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C4; calculation C5; 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 83

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second strength is demonstrated capital-market access. Uniti has raised almost USD 3 billion through asset securitizations and priced the July 2026 notes at a weighted average coupon of about 6.18%, so the build can be financed while the market stays open, though each issue moves assets away from other creditors.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third strength is contracted and growing fiber demand. Consumer fiber revenue grew 19% pro forma in Q2 2026, Fiber Infrastructure new bookings reached a record USD 2.2 million of monthly recurring revenue, and remaining performance obligations were about USD 2.3 billion, which supports higher-quality recurring earnings once the legacy base stabilizes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fourth strength is limited interest-rate exposure. Only USD 345.0 million of floating-rate debt is unhedged and a 100 bp rise would add USD 3.5 million of annual interest, so cash interest is largely fixed and predictable against a base of fixed coupons.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fifth strength is scale and customer diversification. No customer exceeds 10% of revenue after the merger and Kinetic's contribution margin stayed above 42% in each of the last three quarters, so no single contract or customer decides debt service.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first weakness is negative free cash flow funded by debt. The first-half outflow of USD 459.8 million and net debt issuance of USD 1,142.6 million mean leverage cannot fall through cash generation, so creditors rely on market access until the build ends.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second weakness is shrinking recurring service revenue. Pro forma service revenue fell 8.93% in Q2 2026 while sales-type lease revenue masked the decline in total revenue, so the base that services the debt is smaller than headline revenue suggests.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third weakness is high leverage and thin cover. Total debt of 7.13x adjusted EBITDA and cash interest cover of 1.94x leave little room if second-half earnings come in at the implied USD 676.3 million, where cover on net interest would be 1.61x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C7; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fourth weakness is a heavy back-ended wall that rests on securitization. USD 7,360.1 million, or 68.91% of principal, falls in 2031 to 2033, and ring-fenced notes of USD 1,799.1 million, plus USD 1,140.7 million issued in July 2026, give the restricted group less collateral and weaker cover of 1.82x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C5; calculation C8; calculation C9; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 50–54

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fifth weakness is preferred stock and subsidy execution. The preferred stock takes about USD 63.25 million a year and steps up to a 16% cap, and missed completion milestones for rural broadband awards and uncontracted federal awards leave subsidy income uncertain.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C11; calculation C17; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_unit-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-K_2025-12-31_unit-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 106; 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 81–82

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale is a support and competitive position is mixed. Revenue of USD 3,537.1 million over the trailing twelve months and a national fiber footprint give shock absorption, and no customer exceeds 10% of revenue, but Kinetic is an incumbent facing cable, fiber overbuilders and fixed wireless, so scale does not protect its margin. Diversification across three segments is real but uneven, with Kinetic at 56.14% of first-half revenue and losing copper customers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C2; calculation C15; calculation C19; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_unit-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_unit-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 47–48

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cost flexibility and margin stability are weak. Cost of services fell by only 35.53% of the decline in service revenue in Q2, the adjusted EBITDA margin swung from 44.72% in Q1 to 39.25% in Q2, and capital expenditure at 100.06% of adjusted EBITDA in the first half leaves no internally funded flexibility, although the share of spending that is success-based is not stated. Free cash flow stability is weak: the outflow was USD 437.6 million in FY2025 and USD 459.8 million in the first half of 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C3; calculation C14; calculation C15; 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 73; EX-99.1_2026-07-30_unit-ex9912q26.htm.jsonl, page 2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Refinancing access and liquidity are average. The issuer redeemed the 10.50% secured notes due 2028 in October 2025, issued 2032 unsecured notes and 2033 secured notes in 2025 and 2026, and has securitized USD 2,939.8 million of notes including July 2026, and liquidity of USD 1,447.0 million covers 2027 and 2028 maturities, but both revolvers mature on December 30, 2027 and the Windstream Revolver commitment falls by USD 50.0 million after January 23, 2027. Financial policy is moderately supportive: no common dividend is expected, but the preferred stock is a fixed claim and securitizations are the main funding tool.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C8; calculation C18; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 23–24

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next twelve to twenty-four months the outlook is for flat to slightly weaker earnings and continued negative free cash flow. Management expects adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,450 million to USD 1,500 million, which implies USD 676.3 million in the second half, and net interest expense of USD 805 million, which implies USD 421.1 million, a second-half cover of 1.61x. Tailwinds are record consumer fiber additions, record fiber bookings and the July 2026 securitization at a weighted average coupon of about 6.18%; headwinds are the roll-off of first-quarter sales-type lease revenue, the January 2027 revolver step-down, the December 2027 revolver maturity and the USD 306.5 million of convertible notes due December 1, 2027.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C7; calculation C13; calculation C18; EX-99.1_2026-07-30_unit-ex9912q26.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2; 10-K_2025-12-31_unit-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 147; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over three to five years the outcome depends on the fiber build, which management says remains on track to reach its 2029 target. If fiber conversion works, recurring service revenue should stabilize and subsidy funding should offset part of the build; if it does not, leverage near 7x persists into the 2029 to 2033 maturity wall. Sector tailwinds are hyperscaler demand and federal broadband funding; sector headwinds are cable pricing, wireless substitution and universal service reform.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-07-30_unit-ex9912q26.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-03-02_unit-ex991202510xk.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C5; calculation C17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A realistic downside starts with legacy erosion outrunning fiber conversion while the hyperscaler contracts stop producing sales-type lease revenue. Service revenue keeps falling at the pro forma pace of 8.93% in Q2 while Kinetic revenue slips from USD 539.0 million and contribution margin from 42.37%, so second-half adjusted EBITDA lands at or below the USD 676.3 million implied by the outlook midpoint and cover on net interest of USD 421.1 million stays near 1.61x. Capital expenditure staying at the Q2 level of USD 450.0 million then keeps the free cash outflow near the first-half USD 459.8 million, which the USD 1,447.0 million of liquidity would cover 3.15 times if nothing were raised.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C14; calculation C15; 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 73–74; EX-99.1_2026-07-30_unit-ex9912q26.htm.jsonl, page 2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The financial transmission runs through the revolvers and the securitization market: liquidity would be drawn down before the revolvers expire in December 2027, further securitizations would move assets from the guarantor pool to the ring-fenced pool, and the restricted group's cover of 1.82x would weaken. Management levers are slowing success-based capital expenditure, monetizing non-core assets, grant funding and further securitization; the sources do not state how much spending is discretionary. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress through 2027 on the stated liquidity, with no default assumed, but refinancing the 2028 and 2029 maturities and extending the revolvers become the decisive tests, observable at the third quarter and fourth quarter reports.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C9; calculation C18; 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 23–24; 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 83–84; 10-Q_2026-06-30_unit-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 52–54

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Uniti presents an adequate business profile supported by national fiber scale, contracted fiber demand and demonstrated market access, but credit quality is constrained by leverage of 7.13x, negative free cash flow of USD 459.8 million in the first half and shrinking recurring service revenue. Cash-flow durability appears weak because capital expenditure absorbs all adjusted EBITDA and the 2026 outlook implies lower second-half earnings. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the securitization market, the extension of both revolvers beyond December 2027 and execution of the fiber conversion. The primary downside path is legacy erosion outrunning fiber conversion while debt keeps funding the build. Business profile against typical leveraged-credit issuers is not established because no peer set is supplied. Further analysis would require executed debt documents, third quarter 2026 results and the net proceeds and use of the July 2026 securitization.
